promise_band.headline: We will tell you if you don't need a roof
promise_band.body: After every Texas hailstorm, someone knocks on your door and tells you your roof is finished. Sometimes they are right. Often they are not. Our inspection is free, carries no obligation, and ends in a straight answer either way — including "this roof has years left in it, here is what to watch." We would rather be the company you call in three years than the one that sold you a roof you did not need.

signature_system.headline: How we handle your insurance claim
signature_system.intro: The roof is the easy part. The claim is where homeowners lose money — and where most roofers stop working. Here is exactly what we do, and why each step matters.

blocks.title: We document before anyone disputes
blocks.body: A full photo report of every slope, plus the collateral evidence most inspections skip — gutters, window screens, fascia, AC fins, fence. Hail does not only hit roofs, and undocumented damage is damage your policy will not pay for.

blocks.title: We are there when the adjuster is
blocks.body: Adjusters work fast and they miss things. Our inspector walks the roof alongside yours, points out what we found, and gets it into the record on the spot instead of arguing about it a month later.

blocks.title: We supplement what the estimate missed
blocks.body: If the scope comes back short — missing line items, wrong shingle grade, no code upgrades — we file the supplement with the documentation to support it. This is the step that separates a claim handled properly from a claim simply accepted.

blocks.title: We close it out so your depreciation is released
blocks.body: Most policies hold back recoverable depreciation until the work is certified complete. We send the completion paperwork to your carrier so that final check actually reaches you, instead of sitting unclaimed.

seo_body.headline: The roofer to call after the hail stops
paragraphs: Texas roofs take a beating 365 days a year. Hail with razor edges, straight-line winds, ice that wedges into existing cracks and widens them, and a sun that ages shingles faster than the warranty assumes. Some of that damage announces itself. Most of it does not — and undetected storm damage is what turns a covered claim into a leak you end up paying for yourself.

The hard part is rarely the roof. It is the claim. Homeowners across DFW describe the same experience: an adjuster who moves fast and misses damage, an estimate that comes back short, confusion about actual cash value versus replacement cost, and nobody in their corner who can explain recoverable depreciation. That gap is the reason Results Roofing exists — and it is why 181 of our Google reviews mention insurance claim help specifically.

We serve Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, Austin, San Antonio and Atlanta, with additional offices in College Station, Wilmington, Raleigh and North Myrtle Beach. Every one is a real address with local crews. If your neighborhood was hit, start with a free inspection — it costs nothing, obligates you to nothing, and you will get a straight answer about whether filing is worth it at all.

Emergency tarping and around-the-clock storm response
GAF material and workmanship warranties in writing

faqs.q: A roofer knocked on my door and said I need a new roof. Do I?
faqs.a: Maybe, and maybe not. After a hailstorm, crews from all over the country work Texas neighborhoods, and not all of them are careful about what they tell you. Get a second opinion from a company with a local address you can drive to. Our inspection is free and carries no obligation — if your roof has years left in it, we will tell you that and show you the photos.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a hail or wind claim?
faqs.a: Less time than most people assume. Texas homeowners policies generally require you to report a loss promptly, and many set an outside limit of roughly a year from the date of the storm — but the exact window is set by your policy, so read yours or ask your agent. The practical risk is different: wait long enough and the carrier can argue the damage is old or pre-existing. If your area was hit, get it inspected and documented while the date of loss is still clear.

faqs.q: A contractor offered to cover my deductible. Is that allowed?
faqs.a: No. Texas law prohibits a contractor from paying, rebating, waiving, or absorbing any part of your insurance deductible, and the Texas Department of Insurance publishes guidance saying so. It is a red flag rather than a favor — if someone offers it, it is worth asking what else they are willing to misrepresent to your carrier.

faqs.q: What is the difference between ACV and RCV on my claim?
faqs.a: Actual cash value is what your roof is worth today, after depreciation for age. Replacement cost value is what it costs to put a new one on. On an RCV policy the carrier typically issues the ACV amount first, minus your deductible, and holds back the depreciation until the work is certified complete. That final payment is called recoverable depreciation, and we file the completion paperwork so it actually gets released.

faqs.q: Will filing a claim raise my premium or get me dropped?
faqs.a: We are roofers, not your agent, so ask them about your specific policy — but two things are broadly true in this market. Premiums and wind/hail deductibles have been climbing across DFW whether or not you file. And letting a roof age out without ever filing carries its own cost: carriers increasingly decline coverage on older roofs, which can leave you paying for a full replacement out of pocket.

faqs.q: Do you actually attend the adjuster meeting?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the part of our process we would point to first. Our inspector is on the roof while your adjuster is, so anything missed gets raised on the spot rather than disputed weeks later. If the approved scope still comes back short, we file a supplement with the photo documentation to support it.

faqs.q: What does an inspection cost, and am I committing to anything?
faqs.a: Nothing, and no. No fee, no obligation, no pressure. We walk your property, photograph every slope plus the collateral areas adjusters often skip — gutters, screens, fascia, AC fins — and email you the report. What you do with it is entirely your call.

faqs.q: My roof is leaking right now. How fast can you get here?
faqs.a: Call (214) 301-5533. We handle emergencies around the clock and will tarp to stop active water intrusion while a permanent repair is scheduled. Tree and limb impact, major leaks, and wind or hail damage are all things we respond to on an emergency basis.
